To build an RC filter with a 3kHz bandwidth in SPICE and plot the frequency response from 1Hz to 100kHz, you can use the following SPICE code:

```
R1 1 2 3k ; 3 kilohm resistor

\* Connect negative end of voltage source to ground
GND 0 0

.END
```

Node 0 represents the ground node in this circuit.

To plot the frequency response of this circuit, the `AC` analysis is used with a frequency sweep from 1 Hz to 100 kHz in decade increments (logarithmic scale). The `.PLOT` command will plot the voltage at node 2 (V(2)) at each frequency point. The `.END` command indicates the end of the analysis.

The -3dB bandwidth of the RC filter can be determined by looking for the frequency at which the voltage at node 2 is 3 dB below the maximum value. The -3dB bandwidth is the range of frequencies where the voltage at node 2 is within 3 dB of the maximum value. In this case, the -3dB bandwidth of the RC filter should be around 3 kHz.
